main_text.l: IV. De nullo ente per accidens, ut ens
per accidens est, dari potest scientia. Explica-

l.i: bimus singula. Dicimus: de ente per accidens.
Ens per accidens vocatur illud, quod componitur ex
pluribus entibus actu: ut album esse & musicum. Dicimus
insuper, de nullo ente per accidens. Nam
ens per accidens est quadruplex. Est vel concretum,

main_text.l: vel collectivum, vel casuale, vel fortuitum. Concretum
est, quod resultat ex duobus naturaliter concur-
rentibus & unitis, ut album & quantum. Collecti-
vum est vel inordinatum, vel ordinatum. Inordi-
natum, quod componitur ex duobus vel pluribus en-

dine observato: talis est cumulus, qui est aggregatus

page.notes: Marginal note "Demonstra-tio quid sit?" sits in the left margin at the line "hoc evidenter". Doubtful readings: "compofi[?]ta" (the letters "ta" are faint); "Syllogismꝰ" (the superscript after "m" is read as the -us abbreviation); "e" before "terminis" is faint, possibly with a mark over it. The first word of the page is partly cut off and uncertain. The reading "stè sciri" is a best guess. The notes in the left margin are set in small type and have been transcribed as they stand. The thesis line "IV." is a numbered thesis and is therefore given as a paragraph, not a heading.
